equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at book (SSMC JV, TSMC 38.8%)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2025 trough to FY2035): through-cycle automotive/industrial content growth, cross-checked against the 7.3% 5-year revenue CAGR (FY2020 trough to FY2025 trough) and the 5.5% FY2019-FY2025 CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3yr +10.5%, 5yr +2.7%) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs in both windows and is not usable as a growth anchor: NXP returned $8.4B via buybacks over FY2021-25 and $5.0B in FY2018 alone, so book value tracks capital-return policy, not earnings power. EPS 5yr CAGR of 111% starts from the FY2020 trough ($0.19) and is meaningless. Owner-FCF CAGRs are the honest series: -7.4% over 3 years (FY2022 peak to FY2025 trough) and +2.8% over 5 years, both below reported FCF, meaning SBC ($364M to $462M) grew faster than cash flow across the downturn. The anchor used is the mid-cycle revenue path, not any single CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped: net debt company). Series FY2016-25 in $M: 1576, 1614, 3444, 1501, 1706, 1957, 2468, 2275, 1594, 1961; owner-FCF margin 12.6%-19.8% ex the FY2018 Qualcomm break-fee year (36.6%). FY2025 is a trough-cycle base (16.0% owner-FCF margin at a 35.4% pre-SBC EBITDA margin and 3.2% capex).

scenario_narratives.base: NXP's axes are (1) the automotive content cycle versus unit production, (2) China at 35-39% of revenue under US-China trade policy, (3) factory utilisation driving the gross-margin path toward management's ~60% non-GAAP target, and (4) capital allocation after the TTTech/Kinara/Aviva string and the MEMS divestiture. The base takes the nine visible months of FY2026 (+16%), management's double-digit 2027, and then a through-cycle fade to ~4% growth at a ~40% pre-SBC EBITDA margin, a touch below the FY2022 peak, with capex at 5% to fund the VSMC/ESMC hybrid-foundry model. It does not time the next downturn but averages it into the path, and it charges SBC (~3% of revenue) in full with a flat diluted count.
scenario_narratives.bull: Content per vehicle compounds faster than expected as software-defined-vehicle architectures, imaging radar and BMS ramp across OEM platforms NXP has already won, TTTech middleware and Kinara edge-AI pull through i.MX processors in industrial, and the comm-infra cycle turns. Gross margin passes 60% on utilisation and mix, opex leverage lifts pre-SBC EBITDA to 43.5%, and no inventory correction lands inside the ten years. The 15x cap still binds, so the bull is a margin-and-growth story, not a multiple story.
scenario_narratives.bear: Trade escalation and Chinese import substitution in legacy-node automotive/industrial chips flatten 2027, a 2028 channel-inventory correction cuts revenue 6% and takes the margin to 34% on under-utilised fabs, and the recovery is to a structurally lower 37% as STMicro and Chinese vendors take share and pricing. NXP has to lift capex to protect supply. Even so owner FCF stays positive throughout; the bear is a value-of-growth and multiple reset, not a solvency case, which is why net debt at 1.7x EBITDA is not a going-concern axis.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value NXP as a cyclical compounder of automotive and industrial silicon content on a mid-cycle owner-FCF basis: start from a trough fiscal year, let the visible FY2026-27 recovery in, then fade growth and margin to through-cycle averages rather than extrapolating the upcycle. Charge SBC in full, hold the diluted count flat, fund the hybrid-foundry JVs through a capex allowance rather than crediting them as assets, deduct the SSMC minority once, and cap the terminal at 15x FCF so no scenario depends on a multiple the market does not already pay. Risk is charged once, through the 25/50/25 weights, not through scenario-specific discount rates.
key_risks_to_valuation: China exposure (35-39% of revenue): tariff or export-control escalation, or accelerated domestic substitution in legacy-node MCU/analog, would push the path toward the bear case; this is the single largest swing factor

Cycle timing: the base averages the next inventory correction into the fade rather than placing it; a 2027-28 downturn would front-load the damage and the bear (-6% in 2028, 34% margin) shows the size
Margin target execution: management's ~60% non-GAAP gross margin depends on factory utilisation and the VSMC/ESMC ramp; a stall in the high-50s leaves pre-SBC EBITDA nearer 38% than 41%

Capital allocation: the Analysis JSON's reported ~$3.3B Ambarella deal is not in NXP's filings and is excluded; any large cash acquisition would add its net consideration to net debt (roughly -$12/share per $3B) and must be rebuilt in

Capex understatement risk: reported PP&E capex of 2-3% flatters FCF while JV equity calls run through investing; the 5% allowance is a judgment and if the true all-in capacity cost is 6-7% the base falls several percent
Anchor vintage: fy0 is FY2025 with a June-2026 balance sheet, so ~1% of value is double-counted H1 2026 retained cash; the Q3 dividend ($256M, payable 2026-10-08) is not yet deducted

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 183.00-339.95
data_sources.financials: NXPI_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL companyfacts, FY2009-Q1 2026); Q2 2026 10-Q (accession 0001413447-26-000045, filed 2026-07-28) read directly from EDGAR for the 2026-06-28 balance sheet, H1 2026 cash flow, diluted share count, NCI, equity-accounted investees and the MEMS divestiture note; Q2 2026 earnings release (exhibit 99.1 to 8-K 0001413447-26-000044) for non-GAAP margins and Q3 2026 guidance; 8-Ks of 2026-08-28 (dividend) and 2026-09-02 (EIB facility) checked for post-quarter events
data_sources.qualitative: NXPI_Analysis.json (2026-10-02) for business model, competitive axes, China exposure, management's 2027 framework and bull/bear points; its Ambarella acquisition claim was tested against EDGAR and not substantiated

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for Q2 2026 (254,021k) from the Q2 2026 10-Q EPS table; basic 252,415k. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The flat count is funded: NXP repurchased $899M in FY2025 and $206M in H1 2026 (incl. RSU withholdings), more than the ~$470M/yr SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back ($462M). NXP reports RSU tax withholdings combined with buybacks in one financing line ('Purchase of treasury shares and restricted stock unit withholdings') and publishes no separate equity-award-tax figure, so the add-back is used without an uplift; the omission is small (sub-$50M/yr) and understates the charge slightly.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate build: 10y UST ~4.2% risk-free, 5.0% equity risk premium, beta ~1.3 (auto/industrial semi cyclical) gives cost of equity ~10.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (BBB+/Baa1 senior notes, fair value $10.2B vs $11.0B carrying) and 21% tax gives ~3.6% after tax; ~15% debt weight at a ~$61B market cap. Blended ~9.6%, rounded to 9.5% and held identical across all three scenarios so risk is charged once (through the probability weights), not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842. Operating lease cost ($274M liability at FY2025, immaterial against $11B of debt) is expensed inside EBITDA, so the lease is already in the flows; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. No finance leases of note.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest ($362M book at 2026-06-28, chiefly TSMC's 38.8% of the SSMC Singapore fab JV; NCI share of net income $26M in H1 2026, $29M dividends paid to NCI) is deducted once, in the equity bridge at book value. Flows are consolidated so the deduction is made in the bridge, not in the flows.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Equity-accounted investees carried at $1,142M (VSMC 40% at Singapore, ESMC 10% at Dresden, others) are deliberately NOT added to the bridge: they are captive wafer-supply JVs whose return accrues through NXP's own gross margin, and the ongoing equity calls into them ($243M of capacity payments to VSMC in H1 2026 alone sit in operating cash flow; further calls run through investing) are what the 5% capex-to-revenue allowance is sized to cover. Adding the stake at book while charging the contributions would double-count; omitting both is the matching-asset rule. MEMS earn-out receivable ($50M contingent) ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, three probability-weighted scenarios (dcf-methods routing: profitable US-listed operating company with a long FCF history; no memory entry, first valuation). Mid-cycle framing for a cyclical: FY2025 (fy0) was a trough year (revenue below FY2022; GAAP pre-SBC EBITDA margin 35.4% vs 41.0% at the FY2022 peak), so year-1 growth is set from the nine months already visible in FY2026 (H1 actual $6,677M, Q3 guide $3,750M +/-100M, Q4 at ~Q3 run-rate gives ~$14.25B, +16%) and the path then fades to a through-cycle ~4%. The bear case carries an explicit 2028 downturn; the base and bull do not time one, so their year-by-year growth is an average. EBITDA margin in this file is PRE-SBC GAAP EBITDA (operating income + D&A + SBC); the CSV's EBITDA column is post-SBC. ANCHOR VINTAGE: price is the 2026-10-01 regular close; net debt ($10,976M debt less $3,222M cash = $7,754M, matching NXP's own non-GAAP net debt) and the diluted count are from the Q2 2026 10-Q (balance sheet 2026-06-28, filed 2026-07-28), which the SEC companyfacts feed had not yet absorbed (its latest is Q1 2026) so the figures were read from the 10-Q itself. Because fy0 is FY2025 while the balance sheet is June 2026, H1 2026 retained owner FCF (~$0.6B after $512M dividends and $206M buybacks, ~1% of value) is counted in both year-1 flows and the opening net debt; accepted and disclosed rather than hand-adjusted. Q3 2026 dividend of $1.014/share (~$256M) declared 2026-08-28, payable 2026-10-08, is not yet deducted. Undrawn: $2.5B revolver (amended 2026-02-06), $2B CP programme (nil outstanding), new $250M EIB facility (2026-09-01, Kuala Lumpur back-end expansion). DISCREPANCY WITH THE ANALYSIS JSON: it describes a ~$3.3B Ambarella acquisition 'closed around August 2026'. NXP's own filings do not support this: the Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-28) states 'there were no material acquisitions during the first six months of 2026', contains no mention of Ambarella, and the only 8-Ks since are the Q3 dividend (2026-08-28) and the EIB facility (2026-09-02); an EDGAR full-text search for 'Ambarella' against NXP's CIK returns nothing. No Ambarella consideration is therefore in net debt or the share count. If such a deal is announced, net debt rises by the cash consideration net of target cash and the Drivers file must be rebuilt. REAL 2025-26 portfolio moves that ARE reflected: TTTech Auto ($766M cash, June 2025), Kinara ($307M, Feb 2025) and Aviva Links (~$243M, 2025) are in the FY2025/June-2026 balance sheet; the MEMS Sensors sale to STMicroelectronics closed 2026-02-02 for $878M cash plus a $50M earn-out, booking a $627M gain inside Q1 2026 GAAP operating income (NXP presents 'Other income (expense)' within operating income), so the CSV's Q1 2026 EBITDA ($1,684M) and net income ($1,133M) are inflated by that one-off; underlying Q1 2026 operating margin was ~27.6%, Q2 2026 30.6% GAAP / 35.1% non-GAAP. Capex: reported PP&E capex collapsed to 3.2% of revenue in FY2025 and 2.2% in H1 2026 as NXP moved to a hybrid foundry/JV model; the forward 4.5-5.5% capex allowance deliberately exceeds reported capex to fund the VSMC/ESMC JV equity calls and to converge with D&A (~5%) so no perpetual D&A>capex gap is capitalised. Tax: 2026 EAETR 19.7% (Netherlands innovation box and foreign incentives vs 25.8% statutory; FY2025 cash taxes $581M = 22.8% of pretax); unlevered cash rate ramps 19.5% to 21% as Pillar Two and incentive run-off bite. Working capital: receivables + inventory ($1,274M + $2,557M) far exceed payables ($984M), so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of the revenue increase, ~the net working capital intensity of the FY2025 balance sheet).

bear.rationale: FY2026 lands at the low end of Q3 guidance and a soft Q4 (+15%); 2027 stalls at +4% as China (35-39% of revenue) decelerates under tariff/export-control escalation and domestic MCU/analog substitution in legacy nodes; 2028 is an inventory-correction year (-6%, a 2023-24-style digestion) with pre-SBC EBITDA falling to 34% on fab under-utilisation. Recovery is to 37%, not 41%, because ST and Chinese suppliers take share and pricing in mature-node automotive. Capex has to rise to 5.5% to re-shore supply. Terminal growth 2.5% and a 13x cap for a business the market would then price as a mature cyclical; same WACC.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +16.2% is nine-months visible (H1 $6,677M actual, Q3 guided $3,750M, Q4 ~$3,825M at Q3 run-rate). FY2027 +10% is management's reiterated 'double-digit 2027'. Then a through-cycle fade 7/5/5/4.5/4.5/4/4/3.5 to a 3% terminal: content-per-vehicle (EV BMS, radar, zonal SDV, UWB) plus industrial edge-AI at roughly 2x unit growth, averaged over a cycle that is not explicitly timed. 10-year CAGR 6.3% from a trough base.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC GAAP EBITDA margin: 35.4% FY2025 trough, 37.8% H1 2026 underlying, ~40% implied by Q3 guidance (non-GAAP op margin ~36% + depreciation). Management's 2027 model (non-GAAP gross margin toward 60%, non-GAAP op margin high-30s) implies ~42% pre-SBC EBITDA at full utilisation; the base reaches 41.5% in FY2028-29 and fades to 40% as a mid-cycle average that includes the next downturn, versus the FY2022 peak of 41.0%.
base.capex_rationale: 4.5% in FY2026 (reported PP&E capex is running ~2-3% but VSMC/ESMC JV equity calls and capacity prepayments are a real, recurring cash cost outside the capex line), then 5% to converge with D&A so no permanent D&A-exceeds-capex gap is capitalised in the terminal value.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash rate on EBIT: 19.5% (2026 EAETR 19.7%) ramping to 21% by FY2030 as Dutch innovation-box and foreign incentives are eroded by Pillar Two; interest tax shield is in the WACC, not the flows.

bull.rationale: Q4 2026 beats seasonality (FY2026 +18%), 2027 double-digit lands at 13% and the content cycle (SDV zonal controllers, radar, BMS, TTTech middleware, Kinara/i.MX edge AI) compounds to high-single digits through 2030 with no downturn inside the window. Non-GAAP gross margin reaches 60%+ by 2027 and opex leverage takes pre-SBC EBITDA to 43.5%, above the FY2022 peak, holding 43% at maturity. SBC fades to 2.8% of revenue. Terminal growth 3.5%, same 15x cap, same WACC.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; bear is raised to 25% because semis are the most cyclical franchise in the folder's operating-company set and NXP carries a 35-39% China revenue concentration under live tariff and export-control risk, so a mid-window downturn is a base-rate event, not a tail. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once (60%+ gross margin, double-digit growth sustained past 2027, and no inventory correction for a decade). Base 50%: the nine visible months of FY2026 and the 2027 guidance give the near end of the path unusual support.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
